notes.title: Update v0.2.539 Demo Prerelease
notes.content:
[h2]New Stuff:[/h2]

We'll be de-activating the playtest branch on the 1st of June. The demo is now live, though we're still working on getting a dedicated page up so you can leave a review of our demo. It's been a busy month and we've made a ton of progress. 

[h3]Swords:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Three moveset variants of two handed swords.
[*] Slashing/Piercing and Hybrid movesets. 
[*] One handed variants are still cooking. 
[/list]
[h3]Slash Damage:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added dedicated slash attack power stat.
[*] Derived equally from torque and dex. 
[*] Does not scale as well without specific item perks. 
[/list]
[h3]Magic Weapon:[/h3]
[list]
[*]Called the "Broken Sickle-Root Staff"
[*]One handed weapon designed to use with off hands. 
[*]Heavy attack uses charge.
[*]Short ranged projectile on light attack. 
[*]Provides a way to harvest charge from enemies.
[/list]

[h3]Other new stuff:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Spruced up The Inheritor's moveset, particles, and behavior. 

[*] Instead of dealing extra poise damage, most sources of radiation damage now silence you. 
[*] This includes explosions, empowered melee attacks, and The Inheritor's projectiles. 

[*] Turned on EQS for ranged enemies.
[*] They will now attempt to find cover before reloading.
[*] Will continue to explore these types of behaviors for all enemy types. 

[*] Buffed inventory space.
[*] Buffed scrapped backpack space.
[*] We are planning to add a bank system but this isn't working yet. 

[*] Reworked the tutorial flow again again. 
[*] You now start without the ability to gain charge and unlock this ability later. 

[*] Removed the ability to self-kill when you are inside of a boss encounter. 
[*] This prevents leapfrogging as an exploit tactic.

[*] Enabled world save for doors and other door-adjacent world actors. 

[*] Improved the in-game connect to friends UI to work with controllers.
[/list]

[h2]Fixes:[/h2]
If you still encounter any of these issues hit us up on Discord or our Steam forum. 
[list]
[*] Fixed multiple item duplication bugs.
[*] Issue where abilities would be deleted on clients who joined late. 
[*] Potential fix for issue where players could not see the level up screen in multiplayer.

[*] Getting downed by a trap will now teleport you out of the trap.
[*] Moldmetal dropped on death should also follow this rule. 

[*] Relic bloom bubbles now heal you on enter and leave, regardless if all players are present.
[*] Relic bloom will no longer broadcast that all players need to enter it if it has been activated. 

[*] Fixed issue where enemies would fall of ledges more often than intended.
[*] Boosted the number of enemies that could be navigating at one time, significantly improving responsiveness in multiplayer encounters.

[/list]

notes.title: Development Update 4
notes.content:
[h2]Playtest is now open.[/h2]

The playtest is now live so stop reading and go update/download/tell your friends to play with you. We will keep it up, probably until we re-release the demo this summer. But things may change. 

Welcome back to another installment of mycorrespondance. It’s been a while since our last devblog, because we’ve been hard at work juicing the game feel and clamping down on our features. Dare I say the game is almost feature-complete. Our next run is to make as much content as we can before the game supposedly launches in early access later this year. 

[h2]Damage Push, Knockdown, and In-Air Stagger[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44721706/2d87bd971b82838cb4392bcd1c1d4690c71d617b.gif[/img]

Something we’ve found awkward about previous iterations of the game is the lack of damage pushback from melee attacks. There’s something very satisfying about bonking an enemy off of a ledge and watching your loot plummet into the abyss. 

We’ve added damage pushback to most attacks, and this can be amplified by our knockdown system. Generally, non-boss sized enemies can be knocked down when they are poise broken. 

Additionally, the feeling of getting hit in the air was always kind of stiff and jank. We delight in the freedom of movement offered in our game, but also felt like the player had too much freedom and that spam jumping was always better than dodging. 

Enter the in-air stagger system. It’s quite simple: if your poise meter breaks while in the air, you will be launched in the direction of the last hit and you will pancake when you hit the ground. This can happen to enemies as well. The launch distance scales based on damage and poise damage. We think this feature is really fun and we’re excited to see people play with it. 

[h2]Perks and Abilities[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44721706/1076f72cb15f4dd6f54508a73b360298a1315096.png[/img]
This system has gone through multiple iterations and we have finally settled with an item-based approach for skills and abilities. 

Some of you may remember that we once had a skill tree where you assigned points to the tree in order to unlock perks and abilities. This worked okay but it felt very generic and also kind of fiddly. 

In January we were re-working this system and decided to try to implement xp based progression. (Where hitting an enemy with a mace would grant melee xp, and skill points were unlocked via hitting different levels). Ultimately this system didn’t pan out or play well, so we scrapped it in favor of a more item based approach.

Passive skills have been changed into ‘Item Perks’ which are applied to the player if they have the item equipped. Active abilities are now items that you slot into ability slots. These two systems are fused via the Fungal Mind, a body part that grants a number of ability slots and generally offers a build-defining perk. 

Developing new perks and abilities is really easy within this system and we are excited to expand on it by building out different playstyles.

[h2]Items and Inventory Updates[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44721706/c3a27f3037cca646bec932593f55fe22f2a93c3c.png[/img]
We gave world items new, juicier effects, in order to emphasise the importance of loot to player progression. 

The inventory and equipment screens have been redesigned. Now players are able to decompose items into a stable mold metal item, which can be further decomposed into the xp currency that can be spent on leveling up among other things. 

We have also implemented a comparison tool, though we go back and forth on how much information this should give you. 

Lastly we’ve re-added the backpack. 

[h2]Updated Checkpoints: Relic Bloom[/h2]

We’ve updated our checkpoints to be more bubbly. It’s pretty simple: walk into the bubble, save the game, reset the world, restore your hp and charges. Being in the bubble also allows you to edit your stats, change body parts around, and summon your friends to your location.

An issue with the souls-like formula that we are contending with is that the checkpoints were never meant to be used in multiplayer. In other souls-likes, the host must kick the clients and rest to reset the world. Our game differs from this because we don’t have to re-initiate the client summoning process, the clients are just permanently connected to the host’s world. 

The question is, what happens when I am fighting something and my friend wants to reset the world?

Our solution to this is that now all players must be present at the checkpoint for it to save/reset/restore your hp and charges. Our goal is that this will keep groups of players together and focused. 

An issue that cropped up early in testing this system was that there’d always be that one player who was just not on the same page, lost, or otherwise chomping at the bit to keep going. Because of this, we added a summoning mechanic where whoever is inside the relic bloom bubble can spawn a mushroom nearby every player which allows them to teleport to the summoning player’s location.

We feel that this mechanic both encourages exploration and allows players a quick way of regrouping and resetting. But we are curious about how it will be used and need feedback on the system.

notes.title: Development Update 3
notes.content:
[h1]DREAMHACK ATL[/h1]

Attention gamers. We're going be part of the Indie Playground at Dreamhack ATL on [b]October 4th through 6th[/b]. If you're interested in knowing what we smell like, this is your opportunity to know! We will have three stations set up with the latest version of MycoRelic straight off the press. [b]Use the code "SANDYDINGOGAMES" to get 15% off tickets![/b]

[h1]Roadmap[/h1]

We've more or less decided on the general layout and content structure of MycoRelic's world. In previous devlogs, we've talked about the archipelago approach to the world design. Here is a map that Jon drew for our publisher pitch deck:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44721706/64218107c580c93e38169101deaabf4f9b76e1d5.png[/img]
You will start in the mindless bunker, escaping to crab island. We've spent the last 4 months working on these two levels and they are almost polished and ready for the public. We think that the demo version of the game will be locked to these two spaces, though we haven't decided if crab island should be included or if it should just be the bunker. However our upcoming playtests will encompass both spaces, so be sure to sign up for that when it goes live.

[h1]Playtest Sign Ups[/h1]

Recently we've disabled our old demo for reasons mentioned in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2624080/view/4566175115308261675?l=english]this post[/url]. We've decided to use Steam's playtest feature while we sort out the demo page. This playtest will be the same build we bring to Dreamhack, with the benefit of Steam multiplayer. 

[b]These signups will go live on the first day of Dreamhack (October 4th).[/b] We will post an announcement the day of in our [url=https://discord.com/invite/4HrbMmsADC]discord[/url] as well as Steam's announcements page. 

[h1]Leveling Up[/h1]

In a previous dev log we talked about changes to the level up system and how souls-like mechanics would work in our game. We expressed that we wanted to maintain the discrete upgrades offered by a robotic body, but also appreciated the incremental upgrade system featured in many souls like games. 

Since then we have come up with a system that bridges both design goals:

[h3]Moldmetal & Body Parts[/h3]

Moldmetal is our base exp/currency and is dropped in residual amounts by every enemy in the game. There are also moldmetal pickups strewn about the world. In multiplayer, moldmetal is shared. If your friend kills something and you aren't there, you still get the exp drop.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44721706/5b11d1b50c4edfc00ae544b0542cd24191a86ae9.png[/img]
Body parts use moldmetal to be upgraded, but are only able to be upgraded to a threshold. You are only able to change your body parts at a body part station (pictured above). Each body part has an attribute limit bonus. If your integrity limit is 4, you are only able to use moldmetal to upgrade your integrity to 4. You're rocking junk centurions? You're going to need to find a higher quality pair before you can get past this limit. 

We've decided on this because it makes balancing a zone a bit easier because we know what body parts a player will have access to by the time they get to that zone. It also discourages excessive farming, but this is something we're still debating because we know certain types of players love to farm. 

Luckily there are also vendors who will accept your moldmetal in trade for various curios and consumables. Lastly, we think the player should also be able to transmute their moldmetal to gain spirit charges, which can be spent on powerful abilities or unlocking various pathways through the world. 

[h1]A message from Jon (Our artist)[/h1]

Hey everyone, I'm Jon. 

I work on a lot of different things, but lately my focus has been on designing, modeling, and animating couple of new bosses.

We've learned as a team just how valuable a good boss fight is for a game in this genre. When we were getting feedback on the old demo we were surprised by how many people enjoyed repeating Zizifek (the giant firebird) and Berac (the purple magic dude). I think all three of us consider the bosses of that demo to be pretty sloppy, but it's telling that people still really enjoyed engaging with them despite the rough edges. We know that players will sometimes do stuff that isn't fun over and over because they're chasing a rare reward though. While it's unrealistic for me to expect myself to design perfect bosses that will be fun to fight on repeat for eternity, I do want to set a higher bar than we had previously. Ideally the prospect of joining up with a couple friends to kill a boss a few times for drops is exciting both because the rewards are cool and because fighting the boss is genuinely fun.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44721706/0f9a0cb0bb07714085d607967acf1308cb83ee74.png[/img]
The first new boss I'm working on is placed at the end of our new tutorial area.

From an abstract design perspective we want this boss to act as a test to prove players understand melee combat, how to move around, and be difficult enough that they feel a need to level up their stats. Ideally by killing this boss you've proven that you understand the fundamentals of how to play MycoRelic (unless you're getting carried in co-op).

From an emotional / experience point of view, we want the fight to be the height of the rising action within this new starting tutorial area of the game. The visual design of the boss is larger and more intimidating than the other enemies you will have seen up to this point and the music David composed for it really raises the intensity of the encounter. I try to make sure there's always some memorable feature of a design that players get to engage with. For this one I wanted to convey that this was some unholy combination of the enemies you have encountered already, and that it has this weird goopy mace arm that slings around like a couple of tennis balls in a long wet sock.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44721706/17b6c74e36097fb2214e34e176ca4941b6995551.png[/img]
Blocking out the animations for this boss had me spending a lot of time playing with the cadence of the attacks. A lot of people seemed to like the crab knight from the demo, so I took some queues from how clear and spaced out those combos were and applied that principle to this new one. There's always a couple of good options to avoid damage from each of these attacks, so players should experiment with dodging, deflecting, jumping, and sprinting to figure out what works best for them.
I want the average player to find this encounter challenging enough that it gets them experimenting with the different tools they've been provided with to clear it. More importantly than that, I want it to be fun.

There's a lot more I could talk about, like details about the second boss I'm working on. I think I've given enough away about the game for one devlog though. I'll say that I hope it makes you s*** your pants. 

Stay well.

notes.title: Development Update 2
notes.content:
This one may be incoherent because I've been sick for the past week and my brain is still cooked.

[h1]Demo v2 Release Window[/h1]

I am making the executive decision to move the v2 demo release back a bit to better align with the Southern Fried Gaming Convention on the 19th of July. This means we will probably drop the demo update the week of July 15th. 

[h1]Iron Pineapple Played Our Demo[/h1]

[previewyoutube=kwtnfxkFzQE;full]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kwtnfxkFzQE[/previewyoutube]

We appeared in this episode of Steam Dumpster Diving, and to be honest it could have gone way worse. I think it's an honor that Iron Pineapple chose to cover our game and it shows us that we have potential. It was also somewhat frustrating because he played an old version of the game.(The currently available demo is about 150 commits out of date).

The silver lining is that we have either addressed or are were already in the process of addressing many of the problems he found. There are some broader design issues we are still working on, but in general, the new tutorial zone is shaping up and the game feels much stronger now than it was in the old demo. 

Since then we've received a big bump in publicity, and we're currently at about 1/3rd of our minimum wishlist goal. (Our marketing budget is currently $0). 

[h1]Broader Design Concerns[/h1]

The most important thing that still needs to be fleshed out is the core experience of leveling up and progressing your character. The second most important thing is refining the cooperative experience. These two things are related, as good character progression in a multiplayer RPG involves choosing options that directly benefit yourself vs options that benefit your group as a whole. 

[h2]Leveling Up[/h2]

Leveling up in MycoRelic right now is extremely boring and placeholder. The *experience* of filling up an XP bar to get a talent point to put into a skill tree is played out and leaves much to be desired. We drastically need a more souls-like solution, but I also feel like just copying other games isn't going to work for MycoRelic. 

To recap, here are the pillars of the souls-like *XP* experience:

[list]
[*] Getting incremental exp/currency from everything you kill
[*] Dropping this exp on death
[*] Having one chance to pick up this exp before it is lost forever
[*] Spending it on attribute upgrades at any checkpoint 
[*] Trading it to buy items/upgrade gear at special vendors
[/list]

It is an extremely simple system at face value but it works so well because it is so integrated into the gameplay loop. Your risk increases the further you get into a level. There's nothing stopping you from farming forever (besides the logarithmic max level curve). 

Here are some design pillars of MycoRelic that provide a contrast:

[list]
[*] Discrete chunks and tangible upgrades
[*] Your body is made up of robotic parts and should be upgraded as such
[*] Your mind is potentially completely fungal, so your abilities should be flavored this way
[/list]

At this time I do not have some unifying design doodle or strong solution to this, but I do think the direction we are headed involves having a "body upgrade currency" and a "mind upgrade currency." 

[h2]The Cooperative Experience [/h2]

It is difficult to make a game that plays well in both solo and cooperative configurations. We don't want to just spawn more enemies or make enemies have more health in coop. Ideally there are mechanical changes that make cooperation rewarding and challenging. 

Something that we think is working for us is having a "downed" state in coop, where you can be picked up by your team mates. When everyone in an encounter has been downed, the group should wipe and the encounter should reset. This keeps groups together and on the same page.

The other mechanic that is not hitting perfectly right now is the threat system. I come from an MMO background where there is a defined tank role. I don't think this directly translates to our style of animation driven combat, but I do have a desire to flesh out a tank role within MycoRelic. That being said, there is a kind of narcissistic harm done to a player when they backstab an enemy and it just stands there, staring at the "tank" who is 30 meters away. 

I think cooperation will become more focused as we add content, but we need to stabilize the basic downed state, threat, and poise/stagger systems before we start to add wild abilities. If done right, I think we will hit a healthy balance between a souls like game and a group dungeon/raid in an MMO like WoW or Destiny. 

[h2]Bonus GIFs[/h2]

Jon has been blending in the mines and has cooked up some jump attacks. We're going with an aerial and a ground attack approach, at least for hand to hand, maybe some weapons will break this pattern up. 

https://i.imgur.com/XytA4k0.mp4

https://i.imgur.com/KTIaLHE.mp4

(Idk what Steam has against embedding mp4).

notes.title: Development Update
notes.content:
[h1]Devlog 5-31-24[/h1]

First we'd like to thank all the players who have picked up the demo on Steam since March. We've got a median playtime of 30 minutes and tons of feedback that has helped us improve the direction of the game. 

Receiving this feedback has given us a few major questions:

[h2]What are we even making anyway?[/h2]

MycoRelic is [b]not[/b] a survival-crafting game in a large procedurally generated open world with village building mechanics and 100% science based mushroom breeding. Though we all can dream right?

[b]MycoRelic is a Souls-like with drop-in coop and less restrictive movement. [/b] We've been developing with multiplayer in mind since the beginning of the project. Over time we've found the game is more fun if you can jump, mantle, and air dash your way around the islands. 

[h2]What happens when you die?[/h2]

This question has the biggest impact on the gameplay loop overall. In our first demo, we knew how combat was supposed to work. We didn't know how death was supposed to work. This was one of the bigger flaws with the experience in coop. We found players would die and run back through an empty level, or struggle to get back to their friends because they had a different spawn point set.

Furthermore, the formula of a souls like is that the enemies in an area respawn when you die. (Or in our case when the group wipes).

We have prototyped a few systems in the interim. The first idea was that we would have a series of linked respawn points and they would have to be charged up to prevent enemies in that area from respawning. This system was promising at first, but it proved to be confusing. We also needed more sticky mechanics to keep groups together. 

Enter our current and best candidate for a death mechanic: the life shroom system. 

[b]What is a life-shroom?[/b]

Early on in the game, the player gets the ability to [b]place a checkpoint[/b] somewhere in the level. This ability costs 1 charge (our discrete version of mana, [i]lore friendly name pending[/i]). When the player dies, they respawn at the checkpoint and it is destroyed. If the player dies again without having placed another life-shroom, the enemies in the area they are in will reset. 

[h3]Here are a few design doodles that Jon put together explaining it: [/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44721706/205b4433f3c0d321e9ba4065114fdfbec4066d66.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44721706/42a6aac218eb053cd5bb9c1b76931dfe294760e9.png[/img]

We are still working out the details, but the bones of the system are in the game now. 

[h2]Instead of one big island, why not many islands?[/h2]

Over the past two months we have completely reworked our map from an architecture perspective. This was a hard decision as we had to say goodbye to our old level, but it needed to be done. Reworking the map has had a few benefits:

[list]
[*] Each island can be its own sublevel and we can unload the unused islands dynamically, increasing performance.
[*] Small islands are easier to work with, from prototyping to production. 
[*] If we don't like an island, we can scrap it without worrying about the flow of nearby areas.
[*] Each island can have a coherent beginning, middle, and end. 
[*] Islands can be connected in a way that has a satisfying progression. 
[/list]
In this way our world can grow as it needs to and we have room for modular content updates in the future. Plus there's something to be said about the vibe of a fungal robot archipelago. 

[h3]Early concept of new tutorial island expertly drawn in paint by Graham:[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44721706/36c8307a3a571223bbcd52267c00b20192760ca4.png[/img]

[h3]What that concept looks like today (WIP):[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44721706/86c79a3445b0d4e68f9eb6270bde6de5391ede91.png[/img]

[h2]Where do we go from here?[/h2]

The new tutorial island is almost ready. In our opinion, the new tutorial is much stronger and indicative of the direction of the game. We plan to release the new tutorial on the free demo branch by the end of June. 

It will feature an introduction to the game's core systems (movement, melee combat, parrying, respawning, leveling up). Experienced players will find that we have omitted ranged combat and magic for the time being. Ranged and magic combat will be re-introduced in our second demo update, hopefully before this Fall.
